findings.detail: The diff's deletions (scripts/mergegate_check.py migration mode, tests/test_migration_mode.py, numerous .shiki ledger/goal/plan/dag/worktree records, and the c4815d7a.json expected_pr 291→null / status review→ready revert) are not implementer edits. Branch HEAD (55341e1) is an ancestor of origin/main (c537e21); these files were merged to main after the branch base and appear as deletions only because the branch is BEHIND. A loop-owned `git merge origin/main` reconciles them; a 3-way merge at PR time will not delete them. Attributing this to the implementer or dispatching a repair cannot fix it. No action needed from the implementer, but a base sync must precede the PR or MergeGate will correctly flag base-file deletions.
findings.title: Base sync against origin/main required before merge (informational, not an implementer defect)

scope:
Register one new `Migration` in `scripts/shiki_migrations.py`'s registry, following the shape of the existing entries (`id`, `title`, `description`, `introduced_in`, `requires`, `affected_paths`, `destructive=False`, `apply`). Its `apply` walks every file in `.shiki/tasks/`, and:
  - adds `"cca_checklist_profile": []` to any task lacking the key;
  - replaces any value whose entries are bare family names — no `-` and no digits, e.g. `['PR','TDD','V','CCA']` — with `[]`;
  - leaves an id-shaped value (a family prefix, `-`, digits: `CCA-08`, `PR-01`, `V-04`) untouched;
  - changes nothing else in any file.

It must edit in place and preserve each file's existing byte layout everywhere it does not write. This is a measured hazard: 14 of the 112 task files are not canonically serialized, so a `json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)` round-trip rewrites files the migration never intended to touch. Insert the key positionally in the existing text — the established safe point is directly after `assigned_runtime`, with no key reordering between it and `cca_checklist_profile` — rather than reserializing. Honour the `dry_run` flag the `apply` signature already carries.

This task does NOT apply the migration to this repository's mirror and does not change any file under `.shiki/`. It only registers the function.

Add `tests/test_checklist_profile_migration.py` running the migration over a temporary fixture tree, not over the real mirror: a task lacking the key gains `[]`; a prefix-shaped value becomes `[]`; an id-shaped value is untouched; an already-`[]` value is untouched; a non-canonically serialized file (unsorted keys, no trailing newline) keeps its layout except for the inserted key; no other key's value changes anywhere; running it twice produces no second diff; `dry_run=True` writes nothing.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `cca_checklist_profile` cannot be promoted to a required field because 104 of 112 task files do not carry it, and 8 carry a value the gate cannot match.
  Measured 2026-08-01 by driving the real reader: `checklist_profile_coverage_failures(task, verdict)` against a verdict in which every checklist item passes returns four blocking reasons for `['PR','TDD','V','CCA']` — 'CCA checklist profile id PR is missing from the verdict checklist', and likewise for TDD, V and CCA — and returns `[]` for `[]` and for `['CCA-08']`. So the prefix form blocks a fully passing verdict and expresses nothing anyone intended. One of the 8 is LIVE at status=review (T-20260613T095433721787Z-8d6b04d5) and is unmergeable today for this reason.
  Formatting landmine, measured: 14 of 112 task files differ from `json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n'`. Reserializing churns them, and the diff then no longer equals a minimal expectation — which, once the migration mode judges by exact equality, is not merely ugly but a blocking mismatch.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: an in-place migration that inserts the key after `assigned_runtime` and rewrites only bare-family values.
  Reproducible when: the migration is idempotent over a fixture tree and leaves non-canonical files byte-identical apart from the inserted key.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-08-05). Registering a migration necessarily makes `validate_shiki` raise 'committed repository must not have pending migrations' (`validate_shiki.py:674`) until the migration is recorded as applied, so this task MUST also record it in `.shiki/migrations/state.json` — now in its locks, and the two `.shiki` non-goals that forbade it are removed. `scripts/test_shiki_migrations.sh` is also in the locks: it asserts `applied_count = 5`, which a sixth registered-and-applied migration turns into `test 6 = 5`, reddening both that suite and `test_shiki_init.sh`.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Register the cca_checklist_profile backfill as a migration
